known_bad.what: The route-message-census gate FAILS on innovus.log9 with `1 NET(S) WITH NO GLOBAL ROUTE ... RAMCLD0WDATA_123` and `the router DECLINED open nets (4 open nets)`. Every one of those hits is an ECHOED TCL COMMENT: Innovus writes its own Tcl source into the log, and 4_route.tcl carries a comment block -- added after rzG to document that defect -- quoting the exact strings the census greps for. Hits are at innovus.log9 lines 24111-24117 (all '#'-prefixed) and line 24221 ('@file 1633: #'). Filtering comment echoes leaves NO occurrence: grep -nE 'RAMCLD0WDATA_123|is not globally routed|There were [0-9]+ open nets' work/innovus.log9 | grep -vE ':\s*#|@file [0-9]+:' is empty.
known_bad.decision: Recorded as a false red, NOT silenced and NOT worked around -- the gate still reports FAIL in this bundle and the census tool was not edited. The destructive repair provably did not run on this route: the only EMITTED regwire line is `ROUTE: regwire-repair: no Regular Wire markers - nothing to do` (innovus.log9:24195), against positive controls in gdsrun-20260824-valid4 (`5 Regular Wire marker(s) - ripping up and rerouting` then `Regular Wire 5 -> 0`) and in this run's own attempt 2 (innovus.log6, `Regular Wire 5 -> 6`, `the repair made it WORSE`). Independent evidence that the nets ARE routed: the bit-123 census with 121/122/124 controls, check_connectivity -type regular clean, zero LVS discrepancies naming a cache net, and zero Calibre results at the site.
known_bad.withdraw_when: route_message_census.py stops matching Innovus's echo of its own Tcl comments -- e.g. by skipping lines whose payload is preceded by '#' or by an '@file N:' source-echo marker

known_bad.what: Both M8.S.3 trims open their gap from 1.495 to 1.505 um against a 1.500 limit -- one 0.005 um manufacturing grid of margin. The script's own near-miss report lists both sites afterwards, by design.
known_bad.decision: Accepted. The trim is bounded on the other side by the VIA8 enclosure floor: the M8 face has 0.300 of enclosure against a 0.080 floor (0.220 slack) and the M9 face has 0.300 against a 0.300 floor (ZERO slack), so M9 is never touched and M8 is trimmed by the smallest legal amount rather than the largest available.

known_bad.what: Clearing VIA3.R.4:M4 removes 15 VIA3 cuts and 15 VIA4 cuts at ONE PG mesh node -- the stacked pair at (1031.100, 343.600) on net VSS (not VPW; that net does not exist in this design). Each of the two coincident via masters goes from a 2 x 15 array to a single centred row of 15, and the M4 pad from 3.600 x 0.330 to 3.600 x 0.290. Vertical enclosure of the cuts improves from 0.000 to 0.095; horizontal enclosure is unchanged at 0.140.
known_bad.decision: Accepted, and the PG consequence was MEASURED rather than argued. check_power_vias -layer_range {M1 M9} reports 363 missing before and 363 after, and {M1 AP} reports 367 before and 367 after; the per-interface split is identical too (M3-M4 16, M4-M5 192, M5-M6 106, M6-M7 45, M7-M8 1, M8-M9 3) as is the per-net split (VDD 247, VSS 116). check_connectivity -type special reports the same 778 net lines before and after, and -type regular is clean on both sides. All four reports are byte-identical before to after apart from the timestamp line the tool writes into its own header. The matched control, same script with the edit skipped, reproduces every one of those numbers. Nothing is orphaned. The 0.290 target is not a knob: the deck's wide-plate cutoff was measured by grid sweep as strictly greater than 0.300, and the script hard-refuses any target >= 0.300 because it would keep the plate wide while still costing half the cuts.

not_measured.asserts: these bytes are the layout we intend, independent of write time
not_measured.why: a GDS embeds its write clock in BGNLIB and in every BGNSTR, so two byte-different streams can be the same layout. md5 and sha256 identify the WRITE, not the LAYOUT. The three logo_aponly.gds copies in this project all differ in md5 at identical size for exactly this reason. PARTLY CLOSED 2026-08-26 for the PROVENANCE leg, and the tool's limit is now on the record: gds_canonical_hash.py preserves record ORDER, and re-streaming the very database that wrote the shipped _pgeco stream produces a DIFFERENT canonical hash -- 26,842 differing bytes, of which 12,600 are BGNLIB/BGNSTR clocks and 14,242 decode as padring filler SREFs (PFILLER5_G, PFILLER20_G, PCORNER_G) emitted in a different sequence in the top cell. An order-insensitive element-multiset digest over both streams returns IDENTICAL for all 2,267 structures and all 6,210,067 elements, top cell included (5,195,878 elements, digest dc5de33f4716c9b3492f570cd7f5d496 both sides). So the layout is the same and the canonical hash is order-sensitive in a way write_stream is not deterministic about. What is still NOT measured is a geometric arbiter (KLayout XOR) on the SHIPPED bytes.
